title: Rabbi Elazar ben Matya
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: (A Tanna mentioned in the Mishnah.) He was one of the great students of the generation of Yavneh, as in Shekalim, beginning of chapter 5: in Yavneh there were four who knew seventy languages, and these are they: Ben Azzai, Ben Zoma, Ben Chakhinai and Rabbi Elazar ben Matya. In Maaser Sheni 2:4 they said: “Students before the sages: Chanina ben Chakhinai and Rabbi Elazar bar Matya.” But in Sanhedrin 17b he is not counted. In Tosefta Berakhot, chapter 4: an incident of four elders who were sitting in the gatehouse of Rabbi Yehoshua, and these are they: Elazar ben Matya, Chanina ben Chakhinai, Shimon ben Azzai and Shimon HaTeimani, and they were occupied with what Rabbi Akiva had taught them; and there it is implied that he also attended Rabbi Tarfon.

He is mentioned in Mishnah Yevamot 10:3: “This Rabbi Elazar ben Matya expounded: ‘And a woman divorced from her husband’ — and not from one who is not her husband.” In the Gemara there, 94a, Rav said of him: “He should have expounded a pearl, and he expounded a potsherd.”

Likewise he is mentioned in a baraita in Pesachim 79b, disagreeing with the sages and holding that an individual does not tip the community toward impurity; and in Sotah 34a: “Rabbi Yose said: Abba Chalafta, Rabbi Elazar ben Matya and Chananyah ben Chakhinai stood on those stones that Joshua set up in the Jordan.” In Tosefta Sotah, chapter 2, Rabbi Yehudah ben Beteira speaks in his name; Hyman concludes that it must be the second Rabbi Yehudah ben Beteira.
What Yuchasin wishes to say, that he is the son of Matya ben Charash, Hyman rejects according to the chronology of the generations.

notes.text: The final claim is that Elazar was the SON OF Matya ben Charash, which Hyman rejects chronologically; it is not an assertion that Elazar himself was Matya. Preserve Elazar/Eliezer abbreviation by the full supplied Elazar heading and the explicit Elazar in the Tosefta quotation. The second YehudahbenBeteira inference remains Hyman’s.

The consulted Sotah 34a attributes the stones report to Rabbi Yehudah and names Rabbi Eliezer ben Matya, where Hyman prints Rabbi Yose and Elazar. The supplied body and current note remain intact with this explicit witness difference. The second Yehudah ben Beteira inference and rejection of parentage from Matya ben Charash remain Hyman’s chronological arguments.
